class.name: TreeGenerator
class.brief_description: Grows trees and woody shrubs with a self-organizing growth model, and places them as species and forest stands.
class.description: Grows a tree year by year with the self-organizing model of Palubicki et al. 2009: buds compete for light in a shadow-propagation grid, vigor is split between each axis and its laterals by the Borchert-Honda model, and branches that stay in shade are shed, some kept as dead wood. The developmental parameters (apical dominance and control, tropisms, bud fate) follow Stava et al. 2014, and branch radii follow the pipe model. [method generate] returns an [ArrayMesh] with a bark surface and a leaves or needles surface; the measurements ([method get_height], [method get_crown_radius], [method get_crown_base]) describe the last tree grown. Each [enum Preset] is a European species with its own parameters and its habitat. [member forest_shade] grows the tree among neighbours [member forest_spacing] apart (tall, narrow crown, high crown base) instead of in the open. For placement, [method make_species] returns a [PlantSpecies] with generated variants, climate rules and canopy values, and [method make_stand] and [method make_woodland] return [Biome]s for [VegetationField3D]: stand-grown canopy trees first, open-grown trees in the gaps and at the edges, then the shrub layer.

method.name: apply_habitat
method.description: Sets the climate, terrain and water rules of the current [member preset] on [param species]: annual and January temperature, the dry end of precipitation and aridity, slope, soil depth, no growth in water, and for alder and willow the distance to water. Ranges have soft edges.

method.name: clear_cache
method.description: Frees the meshes kept by [method make_species], [method make_stand] and [method make_woodland].

method.name: generate
method.description: Grows the tree of the current [member preset], [member seed] and parameters, and returns its mesh. The same settings always give the same tree.

method.name: get_bole_height
method.description: Clear bole of the last tree grown: the height of the lowest live limb over 2 cm thick leaving a stem. Stand-grown trees self-prune to a long clear bole.

method.name: get_crown_base
method.description: Height of the lowest foliage of the last tree grown (2nd percentile of leaf heights), in metres.

method.name: get_crown_radius
method.description: Crown radius of the last tree grown (the drip line: 95th percentile of the horizontal reach of the foliage), in metres.

method.name: get_dead_branch_count
method.description: Shed branches kept as dead wood on the last tree grown.

method.name: get_generation_usec
method.description: Time the last [method generate] took, in microseconds.

method.name: get_foliage_profile
method.description: Mean horizontal reach (metres from the stem) of the leafy shoots of the last tree grown, in [param bins] equal height slices from the ground to the top. A slice with no foliage reads 0.

method.name: get_height
method.description: Height of the last tree grown, in metres.

method.name: get_internode_count
method.description: Internodes (stem segments) of the last tree grown.

method.name: get_leaf_area_index
method.description: Leaf area of the last broadleaf tree grown divided by its crown's ground area. The mesh is thinned to at most 5.5, the average of temperate broadleaf crowns. Zero for conifers.

method.name: get_leaf_count
method.description: Leaves or needles of the last tree grown.

method.name: get_shed_count
method.description: Branches shed while the last tree grew.

method.name: make_species
method.description: Returns a [PlantSpecies] of the current [member preset]: [param variants] meshes (seeds derived from [member seed]), the preset's habitat ([method apply_habitat]), canopy radius and opacity for shade, spacing and footprint. [param stand_grown] grows the trees as in a closed stand; otherwise they are open-grown and keep to light gaps through a shade rule. With [param variants] 0 the species has no meshes but is measured, for placement maps. Meshes are cached per preset and form.

method.name: make_stand
method.description: Returns a [Biome] for one [enum Stand], in placement order: canopy trees (stand-grown; a second species shares the ground through complementary patches), open-grown trees in gaps, then shrubs limited by shade. Each species carries its habitat, narrowed to the stand's belt where the stand has one.

method.name: make_woodland
method.description: Returns one [Biome] with every woodland stand of [param region]. Europe (all but [constant STAND_HEDGEROW]): riparian, subalpine, montane conifer, beech, oak mixed and pine heath. North America: pine-hemlock, northern hardwood and eastern oak. Canopy trees of all stands come first. Climate rules keep each stand to its belt; where belts overlap, later stands only fill the gaps earlier crowns leave. Append floor species after it.

members.member: Vigor factor per branching order (Stava 2014): below 1, branches grow less the further they are from the leader, which keeps conifers excurrent.
Borchert-Honda lambda in the first years: the share of vigor the main axis keeps over its laterals.
Borchert-Honda lambda once the tree reaches [member maturity]; decurrent broadleaves drop it to spread their crowns.
Bark colour (vertex colour of the bark surface).
Chance a year of a new stem sprouting from the base (coppice shrubs).
Angle between a lateral bud and its parent axis, in degrees.
Random variation of [member branch_angle], in degrees.
Years a lateral bud waits without growing before it dies.
Light below which a bud dies.

Excurrent crown shape: a branch reaches out at most this many times its depth below the top of the tree, so spruce, fir, larch and pine keep a cone (Kantola and Makela 2004). Shoots that would leave the cone wait until the leader has grown. 0 turns it off.
Share of shed branches kept on the tree as dead wood.
Random deviation of each shoot, in degrees.
Angle between successive lateral buds around the axis, in degrees (137.5 is the golden angle).
Side shade from neighbours: 0 grows the tree in the open; around 0.6 grows it in a closed stand.
Distance to the neighbours when [member forest_shade] is above 0, in metres: the crown keeps to half of it.
Upward (positive) or downward (negative) bend of branch shoots.
Bending of branches under their own weight (Euler-Bernoulli).
Shoot segment length in the first year, in metres; also the cell size of the shadow grid.
Factor per year on the internode length: shoots shorten as the tree ages.

Shoot length factor per branching order, up to order 2. It changes only how far branches reach, not how many buds or leaves they carry; below 1 it gives the narrow cone of open-grown spruce, fir and larch (Wilson 2000).

Most metres a stem's leader grows in a year (about 0.6 for beech and maple, up to 1 for birch, larch and white pine). It keeps stand-grown trees, whose shaded sides send all vigor up, to real heights and crown depths. 0 removes the limit.
Leaf or needle colour.
Leaf (or needle) length, in metres.
Leaf width as a share of its length.
Years leaves stay on a shoot (1 for deciduous trees, several for evergreen needles).
Leaves or needles per internode.
Years over which apical dominance moves from [member apical_dominance] to [member apical_dominance_old].
Most internodes one bud can grow in a year.
Above 0, foliage is needles on bottle-brush shoots instead of leaves.
How strongly shoots turn toward the light.
Bud arrangement: alternate, opposite or whorled.
Exponent of the pipe model: a parent's radius to this power is the sum of its children's.
The species. Setting it resets every parameter to the species values.
Widening of the trunk at the ground.
Random seed of the tree.
Layers of the shadow pyramid below each bud.
Base of the shadow decay with depth in the pyramid.
Shade one bud casts in its own cell.
Branches whose light per internode falls below this share of the tree's are shed.
Lean of the stems of a multi-stemmed shrub, in degrees.
Stems from the base (shrubs).
Radius of a shoot tip, in metres.
How strongly the trunk grows upright.
Hang of the twigs on branches (spruce, larch, willow).
Vigor per unit of light gathered.
Lateral buds per whorl ([constant PHYLLOTAXIS_WHORLED]).
Years of growth.

constants.constant: Hawthorn (Crataegus monogyna), a shrub or small tree.
Holly (Ilex aquifolium), an evergreen shrub or small tree leafy to the ground; the shrub layer of oceanic beech and oak woods.
Yew (Taxus baccata), an evergreen with flat needles and a broad dense crown, the most shade tolerant European tree.
Box (Buxus sempervirens), a dense evergreen shrub with small opposite leaves.
Sugar maple (Acer saccharum), a tall, very shade-tolerant maple with a dense oval crown.
Red maple (Acer rubrum), a smaller maple of wet and dry ground alike, with red twigs.
Northern red oak (Quercus rubra), straighter and more upright than the European oak.
White oak (Quercus alba): a short bole and a wide-spreading crown when open-grown.
Eastern white pine (Pinus strobus), tall, with level whorls in tiers and long soft needles.
Eastern hemlock (Tsuga canadensis), a nodding leader and fine drooping sprays; casts the deepest shade.
American beech (Fagus grandifolia), like the European beech with a rounder crown.
Paper birch (Betula papyrifera), a boreal pioneer with chalk-white bark and twigs that do not hang.
Yellow birch (Betula alleghaniensis), bronze peeling bark and a broad crown.
Witch-hazel (Hamamelis virginiana), a spreading understorey shrub.
Mountain laurel (Kalmia latifolia), an evergreen shrub that forms thickets in oak woods.
Beech forest with sycamore and ash; sparse shrubs.
Oak and lime in clumps, ash in moist hollows, hazel coppice, birch and hawthorn in gaps.
Spruce, fir and beech of the montane belt (about 1.5 to 6 C annual mean).
Larch and spruce up to the tree line, rowan.
Scots pine on dry ground (under about 750 mm), with birch and rowan.
Alder, willow and elder along water.
Hawthorn, hazel, elder and rowan with open-grown oak, lime and horse chestnut standards; for hedge lines the scene places itself.
Sugar maple and American beech in clumps, yellow birch, hemlock on moist ground, witch-hazel beneath.
White and red oak in clumps with red maple; mountain laurel thickets and witch-hazel beneath.
Eastern white pine over hemlock, with red maple, and paper birch in openings.
The eastern North American stands, for [method make_woodland].
One lateral bud per node, turned by [member divergence].
Two opposite buds per node, pairs crossed.
A whorl of buds at the end of each year's shoot only (pines, spruces, firs, larches).
